bottleneck: Adeno-associated virus vectors can package only about 4.7-5 kilobases of DNA before yields collapse and DNA fragmentation ruins preparation homogeneity. That ceiling excludes large therapeutic genes such as full-length dystrophin for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, and shrinks further once promoters and regulatory elements needed to control where, when, and how much a gene is expressed are added. Dual-vector split-gene strategies exist but reconstitute inefficiently in target cells.
current_state: Truncated micro-dystrophin constructs fit and are in trials, but they are partial replacements. Oversized and dual-AAV approaches remain experimental with variable reconstitution efficiency.

sources.title: Addressing the Limitations of AAV Vectors through Evolutionary Guided Vector Design

title: AAV payload capacity limits gene therapy cargo size
why_it_blocks: It rules out single-dose cures for a class of large-gene disorders and forces multi-vector regimens that multiply dosing, immunity, and manufacturing problems. Diseases stay untreatable not because the biology is unknown but because the delivery vehicle is too small.
